newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand has record Q4 operating earnings.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand has record Q4 operating earnings.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc, a major operator in the hotel and gambling industry, said Thursday its operating earnings were a record $0.50 a share in the 1996 fourth quarter, up from $0.42 a year earlier.
Both figures are on a fully taxed basis, the company said.
Including charges, fourth quarter earnings were $0.41 a share, matching First Call's consensus estimate of analysts.
MGM said earnings were led by the flagship MGM Grand hotel/casino in Las Vegas, where net revenues grew 4.8 percent due to strong table game play, record room rates and occupancy.

Cash flow at the MGM Grand, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, rose to $61.2 million from $61.1 million a year earlier. Operating margins slipped to 31.4 percent from 32.8 percent, MGM said in a statement.
Overall company operations, which include a hotel/casino in Australia, saw cash flow rise to $65.6 million in the fourth quarter from $61.9 million a year earlier.
Operating cash flow margins fell slightly to 31.8 percent from 32 percent.
Net income for the year was $24 million, up from $20.6 million on a fully taxed basis a year earlier.
In the 1995 fourth quarter MGM had certain tax deductions that led to reported net income of $31.8 million, or $0.66 a share.
Shares of MGM were off 1/2 at 39-1/4 at mid-morning.

At MGM Grand Australia, the hotel/casino saw its revenues rise to $11.9 million in the fourth quarter, up 61 percent from $7.4 million a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $4.4 million versus $700,000.
Much of the fourth quarter's strength at MGM Grand Australia was due to unusually high volume and win percentage in baccarat, the company said.
At its 50-percent owned New York, New York hotel in Las Vegas, which opened on January 3, net revenues were $19.3 million and cash flow was $9.5 million in the first 24 days of operation, MGM said.
The company said its plans to develop an MGM Grand hotel and casino in Atlantic City, N.J., continue, with about 30 acres of land secured for development.
